---
title: "Name particles in Google Scholar metadata"
google-scholar: true
format: html
author:
  - given: Frank S.
    family: Boer
    non-dropping-particle: de
  - name:
      given: Ludwig
      family: Beethoven
      dropping-particle: van
citation:
  type: article-journal
  container-title: Journal
  issued: 2024-01-01
  editor:
    - given: Jan
      family: Berg
      non-dropping-particle: van den
    - name:
        given: Anna
        family: Roos
        dropping-particle: von
    - family: Aristotle
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        -
          - 'meta[name="citation_author"][content="Frank S. de Boer"]'
          - 'meta[name="citation_author"][content="Ludwig van Beethoven"]'
          - 'meta[name="citation_editor"][content="Jan van den Berg"]' # non-dropping-particle
          - 'meta[name="citation_editor"][content="Anna von Roos"]' # dropping-particle in name: wrapper
          - 'meta[name="citation_editor"][content="Aristotle"]' # no given name
        -
          - 'meta[name="citation_editor"][content*="undefined"]'
---

The `citation_author` and `citation_editor` meta tags should carry the same
display name as the title block: given name, dropping particle, non-dropping
particle, family name.
Authors are normalized before they reach the meta tags, but `citation.editor`
is not, so the editors exercise the name builder in `googleScholarMeta`.
An editor without a given name must not render as "undefined Aristotle".
